stem.text: Oil leaks from a storage tank at a rate of L(t) gallons per hour, where L is differentiable and t is measured in hours. Measured values are L(0) = 5, L(2) = 8, L(4) = 6, L(6) = 3. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{6} L(t)\,dt \), the number of gallons of oil that leak out from t = 0 to t = 6, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 2 \cdot \frac{5 + 8}{2} = 13 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{8 + 6}{2} = 14 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{6 + 3}{2} = 9 \).

distractor_derivations.A: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.B: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.C: factor 1/2 applied to the first trapezoid only
